Solar panels generate electricity whenever the sun is shining, but that doesn’t necessarily coincide with when your household uses the most power. A solar battery can bridge that gap by storing surplus electricity produced during the day so you can use it later in the evening or overnight rather than drawing power from the grid.

That can help you use more of the renewable electricity your solar panels generate and potentially reduce your energy bills. Some batteries can also be charged from the grid when electricity is cheaper, giving households on time-of-use tariffs another way to manage their energy costs.

However, adding battery storage can mean spending thousands of pounds on top of the cost of your solar panels, and the financial return depends heavily on your electricity usage, tariff, export rate and the size of your system. Below, we explain how solar batteries work, how much they cost, their advantages and disadvantages, and how to decide whether battery storage is worth it for your home.

Get a quote for solar panels for your home

Use our comparison tool to get a range of quotes from leading solar panel installers across the UK.

That does not automatically make them the right choice for every household. A battery can improve your energy independence and boost the value of a solar setup, but it also adds a substantial upfront cost. To judge whether it makes financial sense, it helps to weigh battery prices against the cost of solar panels overall, the savings you could make, and the support available through solar panel grants.



How much do solar batteries cost?

Solar batteries typically cost between £2,500 and £6,000, depending on size and brand, with installation adding around £3,000 more if fitted separately. For most homeowners, combining installation with new panels is the most cost-effective option.

Lloyd Greenfield, founder of Glow Green, a solar panel installer, says: “Batteries are definitely suited to people who typically use their energy in the evening. So if you're a high daytime consumer, it might be a faster payback, actually, without the battery.”

Here, we make use of our connections in the solar power market to answer key questions and do the maths on whether batteries are a good choice for you.

How do solar batteries work?

Like a typical battery, solar batteries can be charged and discharged. In your home, they can be charged by solar energy, effectively for free, or from cheap overnight electricity if your tariff allows this. An inverter then converts the lower voltage of the battery to the 230v your home ring main uses.

For Phil Steele, Future Technologies Evangelist at Octopus Energy, the strongest case for battery storage is still when it is paired with solar generation. “I much prefer it when batteries are paired with solar for that reason because you’re storing your own energy to then use later on,” he says.

You can get batteries in a wide range of capacities, but they typically range from about 5 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to about 14kWh. You can also add capacity and use two or more at once. The more battery capacity you have, the more self-generated energy you can store and the less you have to import from the grid.

How long does a solar battery last?

A solar battery is typically guaranteed for 10 years but can last for much longer.

Is solar panel battery storage worth it?

Here is the tricky bit. It would be very useful to be able to work out how much it costs to store energy in the battery.

Just like any rechargeable battery, a solar battery has a finite life, largely down to how many times you can charge and discharge it.

So in theory, you can work out how many pence it costs to store and then use a kWh of energy.

Once you have that, you’ll be able to see if it is worth it compared with power from your energy company, which from April will cost 27p under the price cap. For instance, if you could store a kWh of power for less than 20p, then storing sun power would make sense since power from the grid costs 7p more.

If you could store it for even less, then buying super-cheap overnight electricity on some tariffs for as little as 7.5p could make sense too, so long as the storage price plus 7.5p is less than the grid price.

But as we are about to see, this figure is not simple to arrive at, and even if it were, there are other things to think about.

To make things more difficult, batteries don’t just stop working after a certain number of cycles; instead, they lose more and more of their ability to store energy.

Let’s do the maths anyway

With all of this in mind, let’s take a real-world example to get a figure, even if it isn’t set in stone, since it will give a rough indication of whether a battery is worth it.

Duracell’s Dura5 storage system is guaranteed for 10 years and 10,000 cycles. If we assume we can discharge the 5.12kWh battery by 90 per cent, that gives us 4.608kWh of usable charge per cycle. The unit can be bought for £2,280 including VAT but not including fitting.

For 10,000 cycles of 4.608kWh, a total of 46,080kWh of power is charged and drained through its guaranteed life. If we take the price and divide it by this lifetime storage figure, we get a price of 5p per stored kilowatt-hour.

You don’t need solar panels for a solar battery, but you will get the most out of one if you do ( Getty/iStock )

This is a good price because it means stored sunlight – which is free to generate – only costs 5p per kilowatt-hour, less than a quarter of the current grid price. If you can buy power overnight cheaply – some tariffs offer prices as low as 7.5p – then buying and storing the power would cost just 12.5p per unit, way below daytime grid prices.

What are the advantages of installing a solar battery?

Adding a solar battery to your home lets you make better use of the clean energy your panels generate. Without one, any excess electricity you produce during the day is exported back to the National Grid. With a battery installed, that surplus power is stored for use later, typically in the evening, when demand and electricity prices are higher.

As an illustration of this, Steele says that if a homeowner gives up the typical 15p/kWh in export income but avoids buying electricity later at 27p/kWh, the effective benefit is about 12p for every kilowatt-hour stored.

This simple change can make a big difference to your energy bills and carbon footprint. By using more of your self-generated electricity, you rely less on buying power from your supplier, especially during peak times. Homeowners with time-of-use tariffs can also take advantage of cheap overnight rates to top up their batteries when solar output is low, further cutting costs.

A battery system can also provide backup power during outages, depending on the setup. In areas prone to blackouts, this resilience can be a major advantage, allowing you to keep essential devices running.

Beyond savings and security, installing a solar battery can improve the overall efficiency and lifespan of your solar system, since energy is managed more evenly throughout the day. Some homeowners even earn money by joining smart grid or energy-sharing schemes, selling stored power back to the grid when demand spikes.

In short, a solar battery maximises your solar investment, helping you use more of the energy you generate, reduce your bills, and future-proof your home against rising electricity prices.

Cons of solar battery storage

There are a few caveats to consider before purchasing a solar battery. If the battery lasts longer than 10,000 cycles, the price per use is even lower. But towards the end of the life of the battery, it will hold less charge, meaning the price will creep up.

The price also doesn’t include fitting, which could double the cost, and bring about a final figure of about 10p.

Then, there is yet another thing to think about – with most batteries, the guarantee is in years, not cycles. So, will you use it enough in 10 years to keep the price per kilowatt down?

Less usage should make the battery last longer, in theory, but with no guarantee after 10 years, that might prove cold comfort.

In real life, batteries may last longer than their warranties, just like any consumer product. It’s just that you aren’t financially protected if they don’t.

Greenfield says: “We think batteries would last, typically, circa 15 years, maybe 20, depending on quality.”

The average home uses about 2,700kWh of energy per year, and so 27,000kWh in 10 years. That’s just under half the 46,080kWh in our example, pushing up the price per stored kWh if the battery dies on its 10th birthday.

If, however, you use a heat pump for central heating, your usage will be a lot higher, and it could make the battery viable again.

And then, of course, there’s yet another complication. How much can you get for selling the solar energy you generate back to the grid? You can get up to 15p from many companies, which could make storing it less attractive.

If you can sell the energy for 15p and buy it back when you need it for 27p – April’s energy cap charge – then you may not deem the difference as worth it.

If all this is making your head spin, and you’d be getting the device to try and save money, then a solar battery might not be for you.

“You’ve always got to be mindful of the tariff because you might do your maths on today’s tariff and then discover that the tariffs change,” Steele says.

But if you found all that maths a fun exercise and you’ve found a deal where you can store cheap sunlight and use it at night at a lower price than you buy from a utility company, then it could be a good option.

What size solar battery do I need?

The right solar battery size depends on how much electricity your household uses and how much excess energy your solar panels generate. Most UK homes use between 8-10kWh of electricity per day, so a battery with a usable capacity of 4-10kWh is often sufficient to store daytime energy for evening use.

If you have a larger home, EV charger, or high nighttime consumption (for example, running heating or appliances overnight), a 10-15kWh system may be more suitable. Smaller homes or those on lower budgets might opt for a 3-5kWh battery to cover key appliances and lighting.

Steele says a 10kWh battery in a three-bedroom, heat-pump-heated home may cover roughly a quarter of the day’s demand in winter, though far more in summer, depending on usage and solar generation.

Remember that bigger isn’t always better. A battery that’s too large may never fully charge, reducing efficiency and increasing payback time. The ideal system balances capacity, cost, and daily consumption, so you store enough power to cover your needs without overspending on unused storage.



How are solar batteries installed?

Installing a solar battery is a relatively straightforward process, though it must be carried out by a qualified electrician or solar installer. The job typically takes a few hours to a full day, depending on whether the system is being fitted alongside new solar panels or retrofitted to an existing array.

First, your installer will assess where to locate the battery. Most are wall-mounted and can be fitted indoors or outdoors, though garages, utility rooms and lofts are the most common locations. The space needs to be dry, well-ventilated, and away from extreme heat or cold.

The installer will then connect the battery to your home’s existing solar inverter (or fit a hybrid inverter if one isn’t already installed). This allows electricity from your solar panels to flow into the battery when there’s a surplus, and discharge back into your home when you need it. If you’re adding a battery to an existing system, minor rewiring or upgrades to your consumer unit may be required to ensure compatibility and safety.

Finally, the installer will configure the monitoring software, which lets you track your energy generation, storage, and usage via an app or online dashboard. Once everything is commissioned and tested, your system will automatically switch between using stored power and grid electricity, depending on supply and demand.

Professional installation is strongly recommended. It ensures the system meets UK electrical standards and maintains any warranty or insurance coverage associated with your battery and solar panels.



How to find the right solar battery installer

Choosing a qualified installer is essential to ensure your solar battery system performs safely and efficiently. Look for MCS-certified installers (Microgeneration Certification Scheme) — this accreditation guarantees that both the installation and equipment meet UK industry standards.

It’s also worth checking whether your installer is a member of the Renewable Energy Consumer Code (RECC) or the Home Insulation & Energy Systems Quality Assured Contractors Scheme (HIES). These organisations offer extra consumer protection, including dispute resolution and deposit insurance.

Before signing a contract, compare at least three quotes. Reputable installers will:

Conduct a detailed assessment of your energy usage and roof orientation

Recommend a battery model and capacity tailored to your household

Explain how the system integrates with your existing inverter and solar panels

Provide a clear breakdown of costs, warranties, and projected savings

Finally, read customer reviews on Trustpilot or Checkatrade, and ask about post-installation support. A trustworthy installer will be transparent about performance monitoring and aftercare, helping you get the most from your investment.



Should I invest in a solar battery?

If you don’t mind taking a bit of a gamble that the battery will outlast its guarantee, and you use a lot of electricity, perhaps through a heat pump or electric car, or both, and you have a large solar array to feed it, then a battery could be for you.

This is because you will make the most of it in the guarantee period, charging and discharging it a lot, and getting a cheap price per stored unit of energy.

Greenfield says: “If you're a working, busy professional, and you're out the house all day, and then you when you get in the evening, that's when you have a high consumption, whether it's plugging in an EV car or running lots of electrical appliances or lots of washing and tumble dryers, and high consumption appliances going in the evening, you'd definitely be suited for a battery.”

If you have lower usage or a smaller solar array, you may want to be more cautious.

Either way, you will need to ensure the battery is properly set up to soak up cheap sunshine during the day, and maybe cheap grid power at night, to avoid costlier energy.

As the grid becomes more dynamic and more renewable-heavy, batteries may also become more valuable because they can respond quickly to changing supply and demand conditions. Steele links that to increasingly volatile flexibility markets and the role batteries can play in balancing the grid.

What’s the return on investment for solar batteries?

The return on investment (ROI) for a solar battery depends on several factors, including your household’s energy use, the size of your solar system, your tariff, and whether you’re exporting surplus electricity to the grid.

Steele says savings are “a lot lower” in a battery-only setup than when batteries are paired with solar panels, and he would “hazard a guess” of around 10 to 20 per cent in some battery-only cases, depending on battery size, household consumption and the tariff spread.

When a battery is installed alongside solar panels, the savings can be significantly higher. In some cases, a home battery can help cut electricity bills by 20 to 50 per cent, depending on how much solar power you generate, how efficiently you use stored energy and the tariff you are on. Households on time-of-use or agile tariffs may also be able to improve savings by charging overnight at cheaper rates and using that electricity when prices rise.

A typical solar battery in the UK costs between £2,500 and £6,000, depending on capacity and brand. When paired with solar panels, it can shorten the payback period of your entire system by allowing you to use more of the energy you generate, known as increasing your self-consumption rate. For most households, the payback period ranges between eight and 12 years, but this can be shorter if energy prices continue to rise or if you make use of smart export schemes that pay homeowners for feeding energy back into the grid.

The financial benefits aren’t the only return to consider. A battery can make your home more resilient to power cuts, lower your carbon footprint, and boost the value of your property, which are all important long-term advantages even if the immediate payback period feels lengthy.

While solar batteries are still a significant investment, their prices have fallen in recent years, and technological advances continue to improve capacity and lifespan. For many homeowners, that makes a battery an increasingly worthwhile addition to their solar setup.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when he struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg-before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawkeye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Picking some set-and-forget budget enablers who have either high point ceiling potential or will return a steady stream of points, is key to freeing up those funds.

Below are five players the Fantasy Football Hub experts have highlighted for consideration.





Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. The Dutch international netted three times at the World Cup, improving his stock further, and will be looking to get off to a goal-scoring start against Ipswich and Fulham in GWs 1 and 2.



Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m)

Depending on the formation TFF managers are using, Brobbey’s midfield teammate at the same price may be the preferred route to target those opening fixtures. The 26-year-old accrued 12 attacking returns last season, and bumped up his overall score with an impressive 93 tackles.



Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

If looking to fit in more big-hitters, a sub £3m player can be extremely useful for team balance, and the Bournemouth defender looks assured of starting having played a pivotal role in getting the Cherries into Europe this season.

Sports.title: Referee chief Howard Webb fears World Cup row over USA’s Folarin Balogun could fuel Premier League conspiracy theories
Sports.content:
REF chief Howard Webb fears the World Cup row over USA striker Folarin Balogun could fuel false PREM conspiracy theories.

Pro Ref boss Webb admitted he was “troubled” after the intervention by US President Donald Trump saw Balogun cleared to play against Belgium despite his red card for serious foul play being confirmed.



And the former whistler conceded his concerns that intervention in football governance by outside figures could convince some fans that the entire game is suspect.

Webb said: “I was really troubled by it.

“A red card was shown and that there was pressure placed by a politician onto Fifa because that was admitted.

“And we know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament and suspended through a process which seemingly didn’t exist before the season that tournament started.



“Where I was troubled by it was that we live in a world now which is different to the one that I occupied as a ref.

“Decisions were viewed as correct or incorrect, based on your judgment. Far too often now, decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media.

“They try to draw inferences around decisions and the motivation behind that decision, born out of no facts, no evidence.

Sports.title: Sheffield United could face massive points deduction after owners liquidated
Sports.content:
Sheffield United could face massive points deduction after owners liquidated

Championship side Sheffield United could potentially suffer a 12‑point deduction in the new season, after the company used to purchase the Yorkshire team was placed into liquidation by the High Court

View 2 Images Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad bin Abdulaziz Al Saud initiated legal action against Sheffield United's current owners

Sheffield United are facing the threat of a 12‑point deduction in the Championship after the company used to purchase the club was placed into liquidation by the High Court on Wednesday. Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud sold Sheffield United to Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen for just over £100million in December 2024.

‌



But Prince Abdullah's company, United World, is now seeking to wind up the takeover vehicle, COH Sports Bidco Ltd, claiming it still owes £35m in outstanding instalments from the sale. United World said in a statement that it had made 'every effort to resolve this matter amicably' but had 'received no response.'

‌



The petition was heard at the specialist Insolvency and Companies Court (ICC) in London on Wednesday (August 19) and lasted around 10 seconds. With no lawyers present on behalf of the club's new owners, COH Sports Bidco was formally placed into liquidation, and the Official Receiver will now take control of the company.

‌



Angus Groom, representing United World, requested the 'usual compulsory order,' which Judge Paul Greenwood granted, formally placing CSBL into liquidation. The company will now be wound up unless the £35m dispute is resolved.

A spokesperson on behalf of Sheffield United has claimed it does not impact the running of the club, however, saying: “Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner. The Football Club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected.”

The EFL will assess the situation and determine whether it warrants a 12‑point deduction. "The EFL notes the High Court's decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited," they wrote in a statement.

‌



"The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required. In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the Club's ownership structure and developments within the wider group.

"As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage."

Meanwhile, a statement from the Football Regulator (IFR) read: “We are examining the court's decision on COH Sport in detail, and we are in contact with the club and the EFL. The IFR can assess an incumbent owner's honesty, integrity and financial soundness under its Owners, Directors and Senior Executives regime, should it have grounds for concern. We are unable to comment further at this stage."

‌



View 2 Images Sheffield United have reacted to the latest news (Image: Maynard Manyowa/Getty Images)

The dispute centres around the decision to transfer Sheffield's shares from previous parent company CSBL to another one called 1919 Partners earlier this summer. Prince Abdullah claims that is an attempt to 'avoid paying CSBL's creditors.'

United World previously said in a statement: "If the winding-up petition is granted on 19 August, as we expect, EFL Regulation 2.1.16 provides that Rosen must be disqualified from being a controlling owner and director of SUFC. He will no longer be able to be chairman, or a director, he will no longer be able to exercise any control over the club and will have to sell a significant proportion of his controlling interest in the club.

‌



"In addition, we understand that, once investigations are completed, there is a real prospect that the EFL may have to impose a 12-point deduction on SUFC under EFL Regulation 12.3, in order to 'protect the integrity and continuity of the League Competition' and 'the reputation of The League.'"

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United World have hired leading sports lawyer Nick De Marco and added: "As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August, but in the absence of Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests."

‌



Meanwhile, football finance expert Kieran Maguire has weighed in on the ongoing situation at Bramall Lane. He told BBC Sheffield: "If they are dismissive of it, then all they can do is quickly show the transfers of the money at the appropriate dates and United World don't have a case. But at the same time, why would you pursue somebody for money if you had been paid?

"There's one of two things that have happened there if the Sheffield United case, of the current owners is as strong as they claim it to be. Either, A, it's nonsense, or B, the numbers involved are inaccurate and therefore it's not £35million which I think is actually sort of, £25m plus interest or something like that.

"There's a dispute about the quantum involved or you know, they have made the payments and for some reason, United World is denying receipts. But looking at the people that United World have got acting for them, I think, is it Jones Day, who are one of the big-hitting lawyer firms. They're not doing it for, you know, the cost of a big issue per hour, are they? They're going to be serious lawyers at serious money levels."

Sports.title: Liverpool to 'make new Bradley Barcola offer' as update on PSG transfer given
Sports.content:
Liverpool to 'make new Bradley Barcola offer' as update on PSG transfer given

Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool throughout the summer, and the Reds are now lining up a new offer to sign the Paris Saint-Germain attacker

View 2 Images Liverpool have made a new offer for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are expected to make a 'new offer' for Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola later this week, it has been claimed. The Reds are desperate to strengthen their front line before the end of the summer transfer window and have identified Barcola, 23, as a top target.

‌



The France international was not included in PSG's squad for Sunday's Trophee des Champions defeat to Lens and his future is uncertain. Barcola has made it clear he has no intention about signing a new contract at the Parc des Princes, though he still has two years left on his current deal.

‌



But PSG are open to selling Barcola for the right price and remain in active talks with Liverpool. And now, according to French outlet RMC Sport, Andoni Iraola's side remain 'motivated' to sign Barcola this summer. Although there is a difference in valuation, the Reds are set to launch a new bid by the end of the week.

‌



Milos Kerkez gives Andoni Iraola verdict as Arne Slot's issues at Liverpool become clearer READ MORE :

Liverpool reach agreement with PSG star as attacking double deal takes shape READ MORE :

PSG were first reluctant to let Barcola leave but bringing Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts through the door has changed their stance.

It's claimed that PSG's valuation for Barcola is now at £120m, a fee that would make him the club's second most expensive signing behind Alexander Isak, after his £130m move from Newcastle.

Last week, PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi provided a cryptic update on Barcola's future amid transfer speculation and reported interest from Arsenal and Liverpool. "We’re working calmly," Al-Khelaifi said. "We don't talk too much. We get things done. All of our players are important. When they sign for PSG, they become important to us."

‌



View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is a target for Liverpool this summer (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Elsewhere, Liverpool remain interested in Barcola's PSG teammate Ibrahim Mbaye. Earlier this week, it was reported that the Reds had reached an agreement on personal terms for the 18-year-old talent, who has given his green light on a move to Anfield and doesn't want to entertain other offers amid interest from Bayer Leverkusen.

Liverpool and PSG are expected to negotiate a fee before the September 1 transfer deadline with the Ligue 1 club wanting a figure between £30m and £45m.

Sports.title: Monaco terminate Paul Pogba contract over injury concerns just days after wife's rant
Sports.content:
Monaco terminate Paul Pogba contract over injury concerns just days after wife's rant

Paul Pogba has endured a difficult time of things since leaving Manchester United for the second time and the French midfielder now finds himself without a club once more

View 2 Images Pogba now finds himself without a club once more (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United star Paul Pogba has seen his contract with Monaco cancelled after just six appearances. The French midfielder joined the Ligue 1 side on a free transfer last summer following a difficult period with Juventus.

‌



Pogba had returned to the Italian giants after leaving Manchester United but saw his spell ruined by injury, as well as a four-year doping ban. That suspension was eventually reduced to 18 months upon appeal.

‌



He joined Monaco in an effort to relaunch his career but having made just six appearances across his debut season, he has had his contract terminated and once again finds himself without a club.

‌



A statement from Monaco on Wednesday read: “Having jointly concluded that the objectives initially set were only partially achieved, AS Monaco and Paul Pogba have decided, ahead of the first match of the new season, to bring an end to the contract that was due to run until June 2027.

“The Club would like to express its heartfelt gratitude to the 2018 FIFA World Cup winner for the trust he placed in the institution and for the utmost professionalism he demonstrated throughout his time in Monaco.

‌



“During his spell in AS Monaco colours, Paul displayed a remarkable mindset, unwavering determination and the highest standards at every moment.

“Through all his efforts, he was able to return to top-level competition after a long period away from the game, while also sharing his experience and expertise with the first-team squad. AS Monaco sincerely thanks Paul and wishes him every success in the future.”

Monaco’s announcement over Pogba’s exit comes just days after his wife Zulay hit out at suggestions that the midfielder should retire.

‌



View 2 Images Pogba only joined Monaco last summer (Image: Getty Images)

She said: “For all the people saying Paul should retire or he came back to football for the money, let me make this clear, the only one who knows when he will retire is God.

“And for the ones who say he came back for the money, trust me we are very good with money, thank God.

Article continues below

“Social media accepts everything. People can sit behind a screen and say whatever they want, insult someone, question their intentions and forget that there is an actual human being on the other side.

“For those questioning what he has left to prove, let me remind you he achieved the dream every footballer in the world grows up chasing, dreaming to have. He won the World Cup for his country.”

Sports.title: Referee chief Howard Webb admits Folarin Balogun red card overturn was 'unhelpful'
Sports.content:
Referee chief Howard Webb admits Folarin Balogun red card overturn was 'unhelpful'

Controversy surrounded the 2026 World Cup this summer after Folarin Balogun was allowed to represent the USA despite being sent off and Howard Webb has now shared his concern

View 2 Images Howard Webb is the head of the PGMOL (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has slammed this summer’s controversial Folarin Balogun u-turn at the World Cup as ‘unhelpful’ for referees. The USA striker was sent off in his nation’s last-32 victory against Bosnia & Herzegovina midway and was consequently hit with an automatic ban.

‌



But that decision was reversed following a conversation between FIFA President Gianni Infantino and USA President Donald Trump, allowing Balogun to play in the last-16 clash against Belgium.

‌



That saw the organisation hit with serious criticism, albeit FIFA maintained they did nothing wrong. Former Premier League official and current Pro Ref chief Webb has now spoken out and suggested that it might have done more damage for referees.

‌



Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “Integrity in football is so, so important. We live in a world where conspiracy theories are abounding based on nothing, no fact, no evidence.

“Of course, when something like that happens and there’s external pressure applied, it’s not helpful because it creates a space for those conversations to happen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“Processes need to be put into place and followed for the integrity of the game. We know suspensions can be appealed in certain competitions and if that process is in place, it’s right that it’s followed.

“Certainly what we saw wasn’t helpful from a refereeing point of view because referees go out there and make a decision based on what they see in moments and that was certainly the case in the Premier League.”

He added: “I don’t think the referee thinks much more about it. They do their job on the day, the VAR does their job on the day.

‌



“I just think that it was the fact that it was admitted post-event that some pressure had been applied and a process implemented. I don’t know the ins and outs of it but at least what we know, it gives fuel to those people that think that those conversations happen all the time and I’m really confident they don’t.

View 2 Images Balogun was sent off against Bosnia but did not have to serve a suspension (Image: Getty Images)

“Anything that gives people energy to fuel conspiracy theories around refereeing decisions is not helpful for us.”

‌



Webb is not the only one to have criticised FIFA for their Balogun u-turn. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters also shared his concern over recent days.

He said: "We worry that about that particular episode, and of course we don't know what happens.

"I don't understand why FIFA doesn't have a very straightforward red card review process in place, like we do in the Premier League, for example. That I think would have would have would have been much a better way to proceed.

Article continues below

"Generally speaking, FIFA is supposed to uphold non-political inference within the game of football. In fact, it's part of its part of its promise that it won't allow it to happen in the rest of the game. So I think it's a big issue, and it needs to be thought through properly."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford 'seriously impressing' club chiefs with actions towards two Man Utd stars
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford 'seriously impressing' club chiefs with actions towards two Man Utd stars

Marcus Rashford's future has been constantly unpacked this summer, but things may now be changing for the Manchester United forward

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has been playing a role in JJ Gabriel's development (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been working closely with Manchester United 15-year-old prodigy JJ Gabriel and prospect Shea Lacey in a mentor capacity. Rashford, 28, has looked set for an Old Trafford exit this summer, but his work with the youngsters is the latest sign he will remain with his boyhood club.

‌



He has not played a Premier League match for United since December 2024, having been sent out on loan to Aston Villa and Barcelona. After the latter decided not to sign him permanently for £26million, Rashford now looks set to stay, despite both parties seemingly wanting a transfer earlier this summer.

‌



Michael Carrick has reintegrated him into the squad and even deployed him in United's recent pre-season loss to AC Milan. While Rashford has not got the dream move to Barcelona he craved, he has not been sulking.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Instead, the United academy graduate has been working closely with the Reds' graduates of 2026, which include prodigy Gabriel and bright star Lacey. According to the Daily Mail, his efforts in this regard have "seriously impressed" those in charge at the club.

Furthermore, it is believed that the likelihood of Rashford remaining with the Red Devils is growing with each passing day. Carrick has already held extensive discussions with the England international, who was given a tour of United's brand new £50m training facility.

‌



Rashford has also been reunited with close friend Youri Tielemans, with whom he struck up a bond during his stint at Aston Villa. Former United skipper Harry Maguire has also thrown his weight behind Rashford staying at the club beyond the summer transfer window.

View 3 Images Rashford has been lending his experience to United's young stars (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

He recently said: "He's a huge threat to have in your team, if he's going to stay with us. Obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he's a big asset to have.

‌



"I've played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that from playing against him, and playing with him in training, he is going to help us."

Last season, Rashford's standout displays earned him a spot in Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the recent World Cup. During his time at the Camp Nou, he racked up an impressive 14 goals and 14 assists across 49 appearances.

View 3 Images Rashford has been all smiles since he started training with United again (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



His efforts played a pivotal role in clinching La Liga, marking the first league title of his footballing career. It is claimed that the prospect of a permanent move to Barcelona this summer remains very much alive.

TEAMtalk recently reported Barcelona's hierarchy remain in contact with Rashford's representatives, despite having already brought in Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon this summer. United kick off their Premier League campaign this Saturday with a trip to newly promoted Hull City.

Sports.title: England skittle Pakistan at Headingley on Root's return as Test captain
Sports.content:
Joe Root's second spell as England Test captain began with his side skittling Pakistan for 171 at Headingley as Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each bagged five-wicket hauls around a lengthy rain delay and a brief fightback from the tourists.

Root is back in charge following Ben Stokes' shock international retirement in June and charged with turning around the team's fortunes after seven defeats and just one win in their last 10 games, across fixtures against India, Australia and New Zealand.

Bar wet weather preventing any play from 11.50pm-1.45pm, and Abdullah Shafique (61) and Imam-ul-Haq (42) putting on a stand of 91 from 6-2, this was an excellent day for Root, with Pakistan rolled in 48.1 overs before the hosts closed on 112-2 in reply, trailing by 59.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson's fifth Test five-for included a beauty to bowl Pakistan's top-scorer Abdullah Shafique for 61

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue completed his five-for and ended the Pakistan innings in one foul swoop by bowling Mohammad Abbas

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, first Test, Headingley Pakistan 171 all out in 48.1 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Abdullah Shafique (61), Imam-ul-Haq (42); Salman Ali Agha (21); Josh Tongue (5-46), Ollie Robinson (5-51) England 112-2 after 25 overs in first innings (trail by 59 runs): Joe Root (37no), Emilio Gay (33), Jordan Cox (23no), Ben Duckett (15); Mohammad Abbas (1-34), Mohammad Ali (1-38)

England lost Ben Duckett (15) lbw and Emilio Gay (33) caught at slip, to Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali respectively, leaving Jordan Cox (23no) - into the side at No 3 in place of the injured Jacob Bethell - and Root (37no) to usher the side to the 7.30pm stumps with an unbroken stand of 64.

The day had been extended after the earlier rain, which could return in droves on day two.

Root - whose first stint in charge from 2017-2022 preceded the fabulously entertaining but ultimately flawed Bazball era - had no hesitation in bowling after winning the toss under leaden skies on his home ground and that decision reaped immediate rewards.

Robinson (5-51) inflicted a platinum duck on Azan Awais, trapping the opener lbw from around the wicket as a wicket fell to the first ball of a Test match in England for the first time in 19 years, and then pinned Shan Masood (5) leg before from over the wicket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw for a duck from the first ball of the Headingley Test

Pakistan battled to 23-2 from 9.4 overs before the rain arrived, during which time England burned two reviews looking for further breakthroughs, and then progressed to 97-3 once play resumed, only for Tongue (5-46) nicking off Imam to trigger a collapse.

The away side lost their final eight wickets for 74 and last five for 21, with the clatter including Robinson bowling Shafique with a beauty that jagged in prodigiously and the same bowler pinning Saud Shakeel (5) lbw after the batter took two long to request a review that would have saved him - the ball was set to soar over leg stump.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan's Saud Shakeel was left to rue taking too long to review an lbw dismissal - with Robinson's delivery set to bounce over the stumps

Tongue's hat-trick hopes dashed as Pakistan razed

Tongue was on a hat-trick as the players emerged after tea having bowled stand-in Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha (21) - who is deputising for Babar Azam (hand) - through the gate and then trapped Ali Usman (0) lbw before the break.

Pakistan No 9 Khurram Shahzad (14) denied Tongue that magic moment, with a crunching cover-driven four, but Tongue snared a fourth Test five-for by going on to remove Mohammad Rizwan (12) lbw and obliterate the off stump of Abbas (2).

Robinson's fifth five-for in the format, and second of the summer, could have come two balls earlier than it did, only for Gus Atkinson to spill Khurram's hack to mid-on, yet Atkinson made no mistake shortly after when Khurram sliced down the ground once again.

This is the skilful Robinson's first Test since the series opener against New Zealand at Lord's, a game in which he bagged a triple-wicket maiden, seven wickets all told and was named Player of the Match, and he bowled with immense accuracy and control here, too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Stuart Broad looks at why Robinson has previously been over-looked for England selection and what his key assets are

The same could not be said of Jofra Archer (0-26 from nine overs), who struggled with his line and length at times - conceding 12 runs off his fourth over - and looked very much like a man who has had a diet of white-ball cricket over the last few months.

Archer, who was hooked after two overs after sharing the new ball with Robinson, should be better for the runout.

Shafique had entered this Test off the back of a fifty in the sole warm-up against a County Select XI last week and an unbeaten 160 in the Test win in the West Indies earlier this month.

He looked well attuned to red-ball cricket - once he had survived a one-sided early tussle with Tongue, that is - as he compiled a sixth Test fifty, from 82 deliveries, before falling to Robinson's jaffa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in quick succession during the first day of the first Test against Pakistan

England opener Gay had bagged a pair playing for the County XI against Pakistan in that aforementioned tune-up fixture in Beckenham but he got off the mark second ball in Leeds with a nerve-settling single and then stroked and clipped a number of pleasing boundaries before prodding to slip.

The home side could face a long wait before they bat again as Thursday's forecast is rotten but whenever play does resume, it will do so with England in a strong position, with Abbas' fellow Pakistan seamers Khurram and Ali unable to match his precision as they leaked runs and Root now ominously settled.

Tongue: England in a great position

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Josh Tongue reflects on a positive first day of the Test match against Pakistan

England fast bowler Josh Tongue (5-46), talking to Sky Sports:

"We're in a great position now but that first hour tomorrow morning - it might do a bit more at 11am.

"If we focus on that first hour, we can get a good lead.

"As a bowling unit, we were very good and Robinson was excellent. It was similar to his performance at Lord's against New Zealand.

"He's an exceptional bowler when he hits his lines and lengths and he showed that today."

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day two picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival rolls on into day two on Thursday.

The Ebor Festival at York rolls on into day two on Thursday and while the main events will provide world-class action for us to enjoy, it is the supporting card that might well offer the best betting opportunities.

The Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap (3:00) is yet another brutally-tough handicap puzzle to solve, but William Haggas may have the answer in the shape of BULLET POINT. The five-year-old won this race last year off a mark of 100, enjoying a smooth trip around from a good draw and winning with some authority.

However, his career hasn't continued on the upward curve as might have been expected since then, with a trip down to Australia ending in disappointment followed by a six-month absence. Since his return, it wouldn't be at all surprising if his connections have been working backwards from this race.

He shaped with subtle promise in two runs in valuable handicaps earlier this season and then returned from another 12 weeks off to run a fine race in defeat at the Shergar Cup, finding just one that had got loose on the lead too good for him. He gets to run off the same mark of 101 here and while the draw hasn't been quite so good to him this year as it was last year, he still looks to have leading prospects.

The next contest of interest is the Mews Hotel Ossett EBF Stallions Nursery (4:45). Three weeks ago, this column put up the Hugo Palmer-trained MIA FANTASIA in a valuable nursery at Glorious Goodwood. To say he had a troubled passage would be underselling it! He got next to no luck in running and shaped much better than the bare result.

The case that made for him that day remains relevant, with him having overcome his inexperience to win in good style at Carlisle on debut before not quite being sharp enough to be as competitive in what has proven to be a smart novice contest at Ascot that was won by the subsequent Vintage Stakes winner Dr Rascal. A mark of 79 seems very fair indeed and he is sure to have benefited from the experience he gained at Goodwood. He looks likely to run a big race.

The final race of interest on the day is another very tough handicap, the British EBF Fillies' Handicap (5:20). Again, cases can be made for so many of these, but I'm going to venture down towards the bottom end of the weights and side with the Ed Walker-trained SECRET HISTORY.

The three-year-old has already won three times this year, with her most notable victory coming in a valuable seven-furlong handicap at Newmarket in July. Raised 4lb for that, her connections took a chance in dropping her to six furlongs to contest a valuable fillies' handicap at Glorious Goodwood and while she ran well to finish third, she shaped as though the test was sharper than ideal for her. Returning to this trip will be a big help to her and she looks to have very strong prospects.

Sports.title: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy
Sports.content:
Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.

Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game.

Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced.

However, US president Donald Trump then called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to complain, which led to the decision being overturned and Balogun was allowed to play against Belgium in the last 16.

Webb said: "I was really troubled by it. I don't know the ins and outs of the process, but what we know is: a red card was shown. You can form an opinion about the validity of the red card, I can understand why it was given.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Geraint Hughes explains what could happen next in Folarin Balogun's red card controversy, despite Belgium beating the USA in the World Cup

"We know that there was pressure placed by a politician onto FIFA, because that was admitted. We know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament, and suspended, through a process which seemingly didn't exist before the tournament started.

"Decisions that had been taken previously were viewed as correct or incorrect, based on your judgement. Far too often now, decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media.

"They try to draw inferences around decisions they don't agree with and what the motivation is behind that decision. But that is borne out of no fact, no evidence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player US President Donald Trump admits he asked FIFA to review Folarin Balogun's suspension for the Round of 16 match against Belgium, following his red card against Bosnia & Herzegovina

"And when you get that situation, it opens up the space for people to think 'this sort of thing is happening all the time behind the scenes' - and it's not."

Masters, who on Tuesday called on FIFA to sack Infantino, agrees.

He said: "We should be looking back on the World Cup, the football that was played, Spain being the best team, and England's agonising semi-final defeat. But we're not, we are talking about other issues, and that's a huge shame.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chief Refereeing Officer for Professional Game Referees, Howard Webb, discussed the changes to VAR that will be in place for the 2026/27 Premier League season

"The Balogun issue stands alone in that isolated incident which is very difficult to comprehend when you look at it. I think it is, again, a self-inflicted moment (by FIFA).

"Why do FIFA not have a red card review process like the one that exists in many other leagues, including the Premier League, where if there has been a miscarriage of justice - not that I'm saying Balogun's red card was a miscarriage of justice - but it can be dealt with on that basis, rather than use a system which is only about the length of suspension which there is no option to overturn?

"That created controversy unnecessarily in my view."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player CEO of the Premier League Richard Masters discusses Gianni Infantino and Manchester City's alleged breaches of the league's financial rules. Man City deny all their charges

Masters went on to say that he hopes the Balogun controversy will not undermine confidence in referees and the disciplinary process in the Premier League, insisting the competition is completely honest and legitimate.

"Coming back to the issue of do people do believe their eyes, I do scroll through social media every now and then and I do bump into some of the stuff that some people are saying and thinking out there," he added.

"But I do believe that fans, when they turn up and we have 99 per cent sold out, and they watch what's going on on the pitch, it's everything that it should be. It's just the same. It's English football, everyone's trying their best, referees are trying their best, there's lots of controversy, but it is what it says it is."

Sports.title: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory
Sports.content:
Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively.

Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action.

Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out.

Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane.

Balding has now achieved something his later father, Ian, the trainer of Mill Reef, never managed. He said: "I don't think he had many goes at it, though, in fairness. It's always one of the most important races of the year. So it's lovely to win it with a horse like this.

"We've pitched him in some good races with the belief that he will do well in them, but he's kept improving and improved physically. That's the most important thing.

"He's really a very different horse than the one that ran in the Dante, physically."

He added: "I think anything is possible, he certainly has no problem staying a mile and a half if he wanted to.

"I just want to say a big thank you to the team at home because it wasn't straightforward getting him here. Everything had gone great up until about declaration time and we had a little hiccup there with his feet.

"Thankfully everyone who looks after him have worked overtime to get it right, and happily it was a 5am decision that he got on the box to come up here. I'm very relieved."

On Item's next assignment, the Kingsclere handler said: "I just do not know at this moment in time. I think we've got to sit down and let the dust settle. We've just won a Juddmonte International, that was the plan."

Sports.title: Spurs in talks over Man City pair Savinho and Marmoush
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Manchester City over a potential double deal for Savinho and Omar Marmoush.

Sky Sports News reported on Wednesday that Spurs want to sign Savinho, Liverpool winger Cody Gakpo and a centre-forward before the deadline, with Marmoush also one of their options.

Talks between City and Spurs are understood to be progressing, but no agreement has been reached so far, while Savinho is ready to join Tottenham.

City have targets in mind for any player that leaves and will aim to replace them with less than two weeks to go in the window.

Spurs are also waiting for Liverpool to sign Bradley Barcola and, potentially, his Paris Saint-Germain team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye before they bid for Gakpo on top of Savinho.

If they cannot get Gakpo, Spurs are believed to be ready to pursue other targets, with interest in Pedro Neto at Chelsea.

Image: Tottenham's summer business so far

There has been speculation that Gakpo could also be deployed as a No 9 under Roberto De Zerbi; however, while he would be considered for the role if he joins, he is not their primary option.

Spurs want to sign a new out-and-out goalscoring centre-forward and someone who can also link up the entire forward line.

In theory, that means Spurs could make up to nine first-team signings this summer, despite having already spent more than £200m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara has questioned why Spurs haven't made a move for Marcus Rashford and believes that he is still

Tottenham have spent more than £200m on six first-team players already this summer. They spent £185m on two midfielders, Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, from Newcastle and West Ham respectively.

Jan Paul van Hecke, meanwhile, joined from Brighton for £52m to replace Cristian Romero. Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka all arrived on free transfers.

'City will want to replace Savinho and Marmoush'

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom:

"Both players (Savinho and Marmoush) are essentially surplus to requirements at Manchester City. It's been pretty apparent through the summer. Enzo Maresca has said that in the case of both players, they are very much entitled to stay and fight for their first-team place.

"But equally, he understands, a bit like James Trafford, when a player wants to play first-team football, and they're not guaranteed the starting shirt, then the club, if they receive an offer that's acceptable, will not stand in their way. That applies to both players.

"City would need to replace these players. They would definitely, I'd say, have to replace one. I think they would like to and would aim to replace two.

"But the transfer window is closing in less than a fortnight. These are big positions to fill so late in the window."

Sports.title: Doyle: King George heroine 'too hot' for Oaks field
Sports.content:
Our ambassador returns to preview the second day of the Ebor Festival at York on Thursday, covering a variety of Group, Handicap and Listed events.

Kalpana too hot for Minnie in Yorkshire Oaks

Kalpana, a brilliant winner of the King George last month, will prove too hot for Minnie Hauk to handle in Thursday's showstopper at York, the Group One Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks (3.35).

The great French horse Calandagan simply had no answer to Andrew Balding's mare at Ascot, where Aidan O'Brien's multiple Oaks winner finished a disappointing 18 lengths adrift.

That was the second time in a row Minnie Hauk has put in an underwhelming performance and I just can't see her re-capturing her best form in time to bridge that yawning gap. Back against her own sex, Kalpana is simply irresistible, even if the forecast rain arrives.

At bigger odds, I hope to see David Menuisier's Inis Mor maintain the progress that has seen her make the frame in both the French and Irish Oaks. This is tougher still, but Oisin Murphy knows how to get the best out of her.

Irish filly ready to step into Pattern company

Juddmonte's Irish-trained filly Livenka looks ready to stamp her class on the Group Two Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (1.50) at York on Thursday.

Ger Lyons' daughter of Bated Breath booked her place in this line-up by taking a valuable sales race at Naas by nearly four lengths, suggesting she's ready to step into Pattern company.

She's drawn high but isn't far away from the probable favourite Libertango, the Albany winner who only narrowly lost her unbeaten record in the Group Two Duchess Of Cambridge at Newmarket.

George Boughey's filly sets the standard, but Livenka arrives on an upward curve and looks too smart to ignore, while Andrew Balding's Moonrise is another big player. She was second in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot before winning the Princess Margaret yet has been largely overlooked in the Ante-post markets.

Oaks fourth stands out in Galtres

My husband Tom (Marquand) and his boss William Haggas can expect a big run from Rhapsody in the British EBF & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes (4.10) at York - but she has one filly in particular to be fearful of.

Rhapsody brings ideal credentials to this Listed race with a Group placing and a course win to her name. However, I'm expecting Ralph Backett's A La Prochaine to take full advantage of this drop-in class.

Still lightly raced, she ran well in the Cheshire Oaks in the spring but stepped forward again to be fourth in the Oaks itself at Epsom on her latest start. She's been freshened up since then and looks a much sounder proposition than the likely favourite Morrophore, who's best form has been achieved on the All-Weather. She must also overcome an eight-month absence.

Satellite the value in big sales dash

It's pretty unusual to see a Group One winner in a sales race but the participation of Sun Goddess in the Harry's Half Million By Goffs (2.25) at York demonstrates the limitless strength in depth at Ballydoyle.

Aidan O'Brien's Phoenix Stakes heroine looks thrown in on these terms and will probably go off an even shorter priced favourite if her Albany victor Libertango wins the Lowther.

Still, anything can happen in big-field sales races so there has to be some value in Clive Cox's unbeaten Satellite Of Love, who has over a stone to find with Sun Goddess but has a plum low draw and a progressive profile to go with it.

She really impressed me in her Newbury novice while I am also keeping an eye out for my boss Archie Watson's game filly Vollering, who has already picked up valuable black type in France and has plenty of experience now.

Bullet Point ready to follow up big Handicap

Bullet Point came back to form in timely fashion in this month's Shergar Cup and can go one better in the Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap (3.00) at York.

Last year's winner was clearly transformed by the first-time cheekpieces at Ascot and looks another winning chance for Tom (Marquand) if the headgear proves as effective a second time.

Ralph Beckett's Ante-post favourite Centigrade looks short enough for a horse stepping out of an All-Weather novice but I'd like to see Jack Channon's Mezcala involved at the business end of the race. The Buckingham Palace winner hasn't been blessed with the best of draws in stall 17 but will enjoy York if he gets that all-important luck in running.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Fisher opponent revealed ahead of Copper Box return
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher's opponent has been confirmed as Michael Pirotton ahead of the eagerly awaited return of the 'Romford Bull' next month.

The British heavyweight (14-1, 12 KOs) makes his Zuffa Boxing debut against Belgium's Pirotton in the 10-round main event, live on Sky Sports on Saturday, September 26.

Fisher ended the year with a stoppage win over Ivan Balaz in December, putting his career back on track after a rematch loss to David Allen in May.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher says he is inspired by his 'Bosh Army' and has his eyes set on fighting for the British title very soon

Pirotton (12-2, 6 KOs) lies in wait next, with Fisher telling Sky Sports: "I'm excited, but I'm also driven and determined.

"The next fight is always the hardest fight, and everyone I fight is a dangerous opponent because they're getting onto this show with Sky Sports, Zufa, with the Romford Bull Army there.

"It's a golden ticket for Michael Pirotton, but it's also my golden ticket because if I win, I get to go on to bigger and better things. I've got ambitions in this game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher reveals what Chinese takeaway order he would get for co-founder of Zuffa Boxing Dana White

Pirotton made his professional debut in 2019 and won his first 10 fights. After dropping a pair of decisions to unbeaten foes in 2025, he rebounded this year with two stoppage victories.

He has never previously been knocked down, but Fisher is hoping to change that.

"You want to get the knockout, you want to get the stoppage, but I've always said from the beginning of my career, I've got to win by whatever cost - the win is the most important thing." he said.

"But with my power, my strength, my explosivity, of course I can draw a knockout or draw a stoppage.

"Once I get someone hurt, I know I can finish them. I can smell when someone's feeling it or in trouble.

Fisher added: "I'm very very excited to show people what I can do. You haven't seen the best version of the Romford Bull yet. We're going to try and show that on September 26."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lee Cutler and Louis Greene had an intense face-off as their fight was announced on Sky Sports News for Zuffa Boxing 11 in September

Fisher vs. Pirotton tops a bill that also features a 10-round light heavyweight co-main event between Craig "Spider" Richards, Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic, and British middleweights Lee Cutler (16-2, 8 KOs) and Louis Greene (19-4, 12 KOs) squaring off in a 10-rounder.

Welterweight Alex MacMillan (4-0, 3 KOs) and light heavyweight Leon Hughes (5-0, 4 KOs) will see action in separate six-rounders, while lightweights Kayla Allen and Fred Pullen will make their respective professional debuts.
